name: Uruguay
summary: Children, parents and a spouse are protected: with one child half the estate is reserved, with two two thirds, with three or more three quarters (Civil Code art. 887). Without descendants, ascendants have half. Uruguay has a trust law (fideicomiso) but trusts cannot be used to override the reserved share, and I found no private-foundation regime.
reserved_share: Legítima for descendants: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Código Civil art. 887, as amended by Ley 15.855). Without descendants, 1/2 for ascendants. A spouse counts as a child when descendants exist; otherwise the spousal portion is 1/4 (art. 881).
foreign_law_note: Not sourced. Uruguay has a general private international law statute (Ley 19.920 of 2020) and the Montevideo Treaties, but the succession conflict rule and any choice of law were not read.
trust_note: Fideicomiso is governed by Ley 17.703 (2003). It cannot defeat the legítima. Uruguay is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations: civil-law fundaciones for public-benefit purposes exist; a private-interest foundation was not found and the rule was not sourced.
open_questions: The conflict rule for succession and any choice of law (Ley 19.920) was not read.
The spouse's reserved share was taken from a summary of Ley 15.855 and Ley 16.603; confirm art. 881 on impo.com.uy.
Law governing foundations (fundaciones) and whether a family foundation is possible was not sourced.
Treatment of foreign trusts was not sourced.
